characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Supra 55 FEG-Scanning electron microscope (SEM) equipped with EDS and Nordley EBSD detectors from Oxford; samples polished to colloidal silica ~100 nm finish; step size 120 nm and 250 nm over ~100×100 μm² and ~200×200 μm²; three scans per sample; TSL-OIM software
characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Mn5Ni in HR+CR shows two-phase (γ+B2) microstructure with higher fraction of B2 (elongated stringers); austenite deforms mostly by planar slip (parallel slip bands); no deformation twinning or martensite.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the cold rolled microstructure, phase distribution, grain orientations, twin fractions and strain localization (KAM/GOS)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku XRD instrument with Co-Kα radiation at 45 kV and 135 mA, beam size ~2 mm
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 15Mn5Ni alloy in the cold rolled (HR+CR) condition showed peaks at Bragg angles corresponding to γ + B2 phases.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases present in the cold rolled and heat-treated 15Mn5Ni alloy

defect_interactions.interaction_type: concurrent deformation of B2 stringers with austenite matrix
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The B2 stringer underwent concurrent deformation with austenite grains, resulting in significant reduction in average thickness of the B2 stringer from ~8 μm to ~2 μm and eventual shearing and fragmentation at higher strain; one typical stringer with near <100> orientation was sheared and fragmented (~35–45° to rolling direction) at two locations. This indicates B2, though an ordered intermetallic phase, shares considerable load during deformation.

interfaces.interface_notes: 15Mn5Ni in HR+CR retains a higher fraction of B2 than 28Mn5Ni, with B2 present mainly as elongated stringers sheared along with the matrix.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Prior B2 stringers undergo progressive microstructural changes ranging from dislocation accumulation, substructure development to fragmentation of stringers during loading in the cold rolled state.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Austenite deformed mostly by planar slip as reflected by parallel slip bands; no deformation twinning or martensite transformation observed.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: At 50% cold reduction (HR+CR), the hardness of 15Mn5Ni was ~20 VHN higher than that of 28Mn0Ni; all three alloys attained similar strength levels after 50% cold reduction. In HR+CR, 15Mn5Ni displayed relatively higher strengths and lower ductility (YS 1665 MPa, UTS 1800 MPa, TE 7%) among the three alloys.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The sound portion of the 30 kg ingot was homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h prior to hot rolling (applies to all three alloys).
Hot rolled at 1323 K; this processing condition is referred to as HR, with final hot rolled plate thickness about 13 mm.

Hot-rolled samples were cold rolled at room temperature in several passes to ~50% reduction in thickness (~6 mm thick sheets); denoted HR+CR. The 15Mn5Ni alloy experienced cracking beyond 50% cold reduction, so reduction was limited to 50%.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Constant cross-head speed of 0.5 mm min^-1; Walter+Bai AG testing machine; tensile tests triplicated and average of three readings reported
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Flat tensile specimens with a gauge length of 30 mm, width 6 mm and thickness 4–5 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 9a (engineering stress-engineering strain curves in HR + CR condition)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: AFFRI Vickers hardness tester, peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s; values averaged over ten measurements

hardness.value: ~450 VHN (saturated at 50% cold reduction); 15Mn5Ni ~20 VHN higher than 28Mn0Ni at 50% reduction

elongated stringers (bamboo-like) that underwent concurrent deformation, shearing and fragmentation at higher strain
phases_present.phase_name: B2 (FeAl-based ordered phase containing Mn and Ni)

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase (γ + B2) microstructure in the HR+CR (50% cold rolled) condition. Austenite grains deformed predominantly by planar slip (parallel slip bands); no traces of deformation twinning or martensite transformation. Prior B2 stringers underwent concurrent deformation with the austenite, with significant reduction in stringer thickness and eventual shearing/fragmentation.

unmapped_findings: The 15Mn5Ni alloy experienced cracking beyond 50% cold reduction in thickness, which is why the cold rolling reduction was restricted to 50% for all three alloys (blocks b0015, b0070).

In the hot rolled (HR) parent condition, the 15Mn5Ni alloy contained a higher B2 phase fraction (~12%) than 28Mn5Ni (~4%), and also possessed a higher volume fraction of κ-carbides; HR austenite grain sizes were ~5–7 μm (block b0026, b0084). This prior B2 stringer content carries over into the HR+CR condition.
The initial bulk hardness of 15Mn5Ni in the HR condition was ~375 ± 6 VHN, which increased to ~450 VHN saturated at 50% cold reduction (block b0045).
The strain hardening exponent n is not reported for any alloy in the HR+CR condition (n column blank in Table 3); n values are only given for heat-treated conditions (block b0060).
Block b0012 lists the third alloy composition as 'Fe–15Mn–9Al-0.9C–15Mn', which appears to be a typographical error for Fe–15Mn–9Al-0.9C–5Ni, as consistently given elsewhere (block b0008, b0084).
